headline: Electric Utilities; Pilot Program for Energy Assistance
short_summary: This bill amends funding for energy assistance and weatherization pilot programs, extends their sunset date, and allows Dominion Energy Virginia to recover costs for certain electrical facilities while allocating some costs to large industrial customers.
supporters: Delegates LeVere Bolling, Keys-Gamarra, McAuliff, McQuinn; Commission on Electric Utility Regulation; Governor Abigail Spanberger.
news_headline: Governor Amends Bills, Shifts Costs, Saves Customers
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger's amendments to HB 1393 aim to save money for residential customers by restricting Dominion Energy's spending on line undergrounding and capping its return on equity. Despite critics' claims, these changes are expected to lead to lower rates for customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Requirements
short_summary: This bill requires water suppliers to report monthly water usage data, including potable and reclaimed water, for data centers with air permits, domestic users, and commercial/industrial users, with an effective date of January 1, 2027.
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan; Delegate Elizabeth Guzman; Delegate Shelly Simonds; environmental groups; water resource planners.
opponents: None explicitly named in search results.
news_headline: Virginia to Require Detailed Data Center Water Reporting
news_summary: Virginia has approved legislation (HB 496, identical to SB 553) that will require water suppliers to provide detailed monthly breakdowns of water usage by major customer groups, including data centers, starting January 1, 2027. This aims to provide clearer insight into local resource use, as data on data center water consumption has often been private.

headline: Data Centers; Site Assessment, Sound Profile
short_summary: This bill requires localities to mandate a site assessment for new high energy use facilities (HEUFs) like data centers, examining sound profiles on nearby residential units and schools, and allows assessment of impacts on water, agriculture, parks, historic sites, and forestland.
supporters: Delegates Thomas and McAuliff; localities and residents concerned about noise and environmental impacts.
opponents: None explicitly named in search results.
news_headline: Virginia Adds Restrictions on Data Center Siting, Noise
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger signed bills, including HB 153, to regulate data centers, addressing concerns about noise and requiring impact assessments for new facilities. This mandates localities require site assessments for new high energy use facilities, examining sound profiles and potential impacts on various resources before rezoning approval.
